title: WSUG: Fix numerous grammar issues
description:
This is a continuation of !6346, to fix
grammar issues in the rest of the WSUG.

notes.body: approved this merge request

added 3 commits
  • f5b2a417...f405771a - 2 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 20c04f49 - WSUG: Fix numerous grammar issues
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/6393/diffs?diff_id=347083886&start_sha=f5b2a41772e35d0141fb0ae58d38a0ef2c7d7a5c)
Again, prefer without the comma
Per https://www.warnell.uga.edu/sites/default/files/inline-files/ieVeg.pdf , e.g. is always supposed to be followed with a comma. If you still think it shouldn't here, I will revert this line.

It's only my opinionated opinion, either way is fine.  I see the logic that you would write "for example, " or "that is, ".  I think maybe it just jarred to see it in a document that otherwise speaks in an informal voice.

My overall goal is to have the most easily understood content and my hope is that improving the grammar aids that.

If you're fine either way re: `e.g.,` vs `e.g.`, can we keep the comma since (at least from that source), that appears to be the  'more-correct' option?
Yes, lets keep the comma - I didn't feel that strongly about it.
I would add the the . but not the , here

Same deal: per https://www.warnell.uga.edu/sites/default/files/inline-files/ieVeg.pdf , e.g. is always supposed to be followed with a comma. If you still think it shouldn't here, I will revert this line.
"You can also"

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/6393/diffs?diff_id=347506365&start_sha=20c04f49bfb785a0e5e04c1ff4a9aca8f8f7eb31#c3d260f5e10c2a7adc987775268dcca104285a4d_551_551)

This is a continuation of #6346, to fix
grammar issues in the rest of the WSUG.
